analysis: The code snippet contains multiple calls to `getLocationOnScreen()` on different objects. The only declared exception is `IllegalComponentStateException`, which is thrown when the component is not showing on the screen. In the snippet, the first call is on `data` without any prior validation that the component is showing. The second call is on `p` (PlayAreaPanel) after a null check but without a check that the panel is visible or showing. The third call inside the graveyard block again calls on `p` after a null check but without visibility validation. Therefore, none of these calls have appropriate checks to avoid the exception. Note: The call `permanent.getCardLocationOnScreen().getCardPoint()` uses a different method, not the one in question, so it is not considered.
remark: The exception `IllegalComponentStateException` can be triggered in three scenarios: (1) When `data.getLocationOnScreen()` is called, if the `data` component is not showing on screen. (2) When `p.getLocationOnScreen()` is called inside the loop after `if (p != null)`, if the `PlayAreaPanel` (p) is not showing on screen. (3) When `p.getLocationOnScreen()` is called inside the graveyard block after the null check, if that panel is not showing. In all cases, the component may have been disposed, minimized, or not yet rendered, leading to the exception.
